heroSummary: The Bambu Lab P1S natively processes Polymaker PolyTerra PLA with exceptional print quality right out of the box using stock hardware. Operating at a maximum volumetric flow rate of 21 mm³/s, the system achieves reliable print speeds up to 250 mm/s without requiring nozzle upgrades.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate (clean with IPA or warm soapy water, no glue required)
slicerTweaks: Set Max Volumetric Speed to 21 mm³/s under Filament Settings > Basic Information to prevent underextrusion at high feedrates.
Adjust Pressure Advance / Flow Dynamics factor to 0.024 to minimize bulging on sharp outer corners.
Keep chamber door cracked open or top glass vented during extended prints to avoid heat creep inside the enclosed P1S.
Set outer wall speed to 120 mm/s while maintaining inner walls at 250 mm/s to achieve a uniform matte surface finish.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Extruder clicking and heat creep clog
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Enclosed chamber air temperature exceeds PLA glass transition threshold (~55-60°C) during continuous printing.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Unseat the top glass lid or prop the front door open, and confirm chamber auxiliary fan is running.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Weak layer adhesion and brittle prints
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Extrusion temperature is too low for high-speed throughput (250 mm/s) on the stock stainless steel nozzle.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Increase nozzle temperature from 210°C to 220°C in OrcaSlicer filament settings to ensure complete polymer melt.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Stringing and whisker formation across travel paths
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Retraction distance too low or high residual nozzle pressure during high-speed travel moves.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Increase retraction distance to 0.8mm, set z-hop to 0.2mm (auto lift), and enable 'Wipe while retracting' (2mm).

faq.question: Can I use cardboard spools of PolyTerra PLA inside the Bambu AMS?
faq.answer: Yes, but it is highly recommended to snap on plastic spool rim adapters or wrap the cardboard edges with electrical tape to avoid paper dust accumulating in the AMS feeder gears.

faq.question: Do I need a hardened steel nozzle to print PolyTerra PLA?
faq.answer: No, PolyTerra PLA is a standard matte PLA filled with organic minerals that are non-abrasive, making it completely safe for the stock stainless steel nozzle.

faq.question: Why is the matte finish inconsistent between fast and slow sections?
faq.answer: Differences in melt temperature caused by speed variations affect surface gloss; cap outer wall speed consistently at 100-120 mm/s to maintain a uniform matte sheen.

faq.question: Should the P1S enclosure door remain closed while printing PolyTerra PLA?
faq.answer: No, PLA prints best with ample ventilation; keep the front glass door slightly ajar or the top lid cracked to maintain internal chamber temperatures below 35°C.
